title: Chocolate and espresso tart
subtitle: a cocoa pastry case filled with a silky chocolate and espresso ganache, set without baking
excerpt: Chocolate and espresso tart has a crisp cocoa pastry shell filled with a rich ganache of dark chocolate, cream, and strong espresso, poured in warm and left to set in the fridge. The tart does not go back in the oven after the shell is baked; the filling sets from the warmth of the cream and the fridge. It cuts cleanly and holds its shape at room temperature for several hours.
sourceNotes: No-bake chocolate ganache tarts became popular in British restaurant dessert menus from the 1980s onward. The combination of chocolate and espresso is Italian in origin, reflecting the influence of Italian cafe culture on British cooking during the same period.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made up to 2 days ahead and kept refrigerated. Remove from the fridge 20 minutes before serving.
recipe.temperatureNote: fan 180 degrees C / gas 6 for blind baking the shell only

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: fan 180 degrees C / gas 6 for blind baking the shell only

content.text: Chocolate and espresso tart is a crisp cocoa pastry case filled with a dark, silky ganache that sets in the fridge rather than in the oven. The filling is warm cream poured over finely chopped dark chocolate with a shot of strong espresso stirred through. Pour it into the baked shell while still warm so it levels itself perfectly, then refrigerate until set.

items.prepNote: strong, freshly made or from a shot

content.text: Make the cocoa pastry: rub the cold butter into the flour, cocoa, and icing sugar until fine and crumbly. Mix in the egg yolk and just enough cold water to bring the dough together. Chill for 30 minutes.

Roll the pastry to 3 mm and line a 23 cm tart tin. Chill for 15 minutes. Blind bake at 200 degrees C (fan 180 degrees C / gas 6) for 15 minutes with beans, then 8 minutes without, until the base is set and dry. Cool completely.
Put the chopped dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl. Heat the cream and espresso together in a small saucepan until just below the boil. Pour over the chocolate and leave for 1 minute.
Stir slowly from the centre outward until the ganache is smooth. Add the butter and stir until incorporated. Leave to cool for 5 minutes.
Pour the warm ganache into the cooled pastry case. It will level itself. Scatter flaked salt over the surface if using. Refrigerate for at least 3 hours until fully set.
Remove from the fridge 20 minutes before serving. Slice with a knife dipped in hot water and dried between cuts.

attrs.avoid: Avoid refrigerating in a very cold fridge or next to the fan; a rapid chill causes the surface to crack.
attrs.fix: Leave the tart at room temperature for 30 minutes before moving to the fridge. Keep away from the back or fan of the fridge where temperatures are coldest.

attrs.problem: Ganache stays soft in the centre after chilling
attrs.avoid: Avoid too warm a cream or a ganache that is too thin; insufficient chocolate to cream ratio stays liquid.
attrs.fix: The ratio of 300 g chocolate to 300 g cream (1:1 by weight) should set firm. If it doesn't, the chocolate may have been measured short. Chill for an extra hour or melt an extra 30 g of chocolate into the ganache before pouring.
